caption_revisions.original_caption: A more certain crowd can keep a middle.
caption_revisions.revised_caption:
A more certain crowd keeps a middle
in 11 of our 20 runs.

caption_verdicts.caption:
200 Flumps, each with an opinion.
A few at the ends are very sure of themselves.
caption_verdicts.why: 200 agents; 10 initial extremists with uncertainty 0.1 versus moderates 1.4, all 50 seeds

caption_verdicts.caption:
Each has an uncertainty range around its opinion.
A short range means more confidence.
caption_verdicts.why: uncertainty is the half-width of each measured opinion segment; initial values 0.1 versus 1.4

caption_verdicts.caption:
Random pairs meet. Enough overlap lets one change
the other's opinion and uncertainty.
caption_verdicts.why: RA simultaneous old-state updates; shared select_pair finds actual initial asymmetric-overlap pair in every seed

caption_verdicts.caption:
A more certain crowd keeps a middle
in 11 of our 20 runs.
caption_verdicts.why: 11/20 seeds retain at least half the initial moderates within |x|≤0.5; caption revised after result was known, original prospective rule 16/20 failed

caption_verdicts.caption: A less certain crowd can split between both extremes.
caption_verdicts.why: 50/50 both extremes; rule requires at least 40

caption_verdicts.caption:
Even with equal extremists at both ends,
a few confident Flumps can pull nearly everyone to one side.
caption_verdicts.why: 48/50 recruit at least 90% beyond one fixed initial cutoff; both signs observed; equal initial extremist counts

caption_verdicts.caption:
Stop early, and a crowd still drifting
hasn't yet crossed the counting line.
caption_verdicts.why: 0/50 single at period 200, mean physical drift 0.550; all trajectories read before period 1200

caption_verdicts.caption:
The authors' reply waited for opinions to settle,
and after seeing the runs, moved the counting line inward.
caption_verdicts.why: same band initialization and seed; prescribed horizons 200 and 1200; cutoffs ±0.8 and ±0.7, a later author measurement choice rather than a change in trajectories

caption_verdicts.caption: Together, those changes recover a frequent single extreme.
caption_verdicts.why: single frequencies original 0/50, horizon only 20/50, cutoff only 13/50, combined 49/50; 1200 is a fixed horizon, not a guarantee of numerical stability

caption_verdicts.caption:
At these settings, a bigger crowd
reaches one extreme much less often.
caption_verdicts.why: N200: 34/50 versus N2000: 1/50; every run stable

caption_verdicts.caption: A small imbalance makes one side more likely to win.
caption_verdicts.why: balanced singles 7/50; imbalance favored-side wins 48/50, opposite 0/50

caption_verdicts.caption:
With their alternative's printed rule,
the moderates pull the extremists toward the middle.
caption_verdicts.why: 50/50 with direct initial-extremist final mean absolute opinion <0.5 and y=0

caption_verdicts.caption:
Hear only neighbors on this lattice,
and neither extreme takes over the crowd.
caption_verdicts.why: 0/20 sides recruit 70% beyond ±0.9; 9/20 unsettled at the declared 20000-period cap

caption_verdicts.caption:
How extremists win
A confident minority can move an uncertain crowd.
After Deffuant et al., 2002
caption_verdicts.why: model mechanism supported by the measured single-extreme setup; no empirical law about people
